subject: Daily AcreetionOS Update -- September 11, 2026
body:
Daily AcreetionOS Update - September 11, 2026

Development team continues refining the release pipeline with recent commits addressing critical CI/CD improvements in the acreetionos-immutable repository. The weekend work focused on fixing release.yml workflow validation and updating the GitHub release process to pass the -R flag correctly. Additionally, a missing firefox-ublock-origin package was added to the XLibre build, ensuring comprehensive ad-blocking support out of the box.

The acreetionos-code.github.io repository received intelligence sync updates for newsletter management and wiki guides, maintaining our documentation infrastructure. A deploy key fix in the GitLab mirror setup was successfully implemented to ensure seamless synchronization across platforms. Shellcheck linting was explicitly applied to top-level scripts, improving code quality and catching potential issues early in development cycles.

Community members can now benefit from Forgejo 16.0.4 and 15.0.8 patches addressing a critical security vulnerability in the software-forge ecosystem. Julia language users will want to note the September release of version 1.13, which brings significant highlights to the programming environment. Thursday's security updates covered multiple distributions including AlmaLinux with important patches for kernel, glibc, and various other components.

The AcreetionOS Discord server remains active with ongoing discussions about upcoming features and user feedback integration. Our GitHub repositories continue to attract attention from the Arch Linux community who appreciate the refined installer experience. Followers can connect with us on X/Twitter @acreetionos and on Bluesky at acreetionos.bsky.social for real-time updates.

Remember that AcreetionOS provides a sovereign, telemetry-free Linux experience based on Arch Linux with the Cinnamon desktop environment. Our distribution requires a minimum of 2GB RAM and 20GB storage on 64-bit processors, making it accessible yet powerful. The project is completely free to download from acreetionos.org/flash.html with comprehensive documentation available in our wiki.

Natalie Cole-Clift Spiva serves as co-leader of the project, bringing systems engineering expertise and deep Linux knowledge to every aspect of development. Darren Clift handles the foundational infrastructure work including Calamares customization, ISO builds, and kernel configuration. This father-daughter collaboration has produced a remarkable achievement in just 1000+ hours of combined work.

The Calamares installer has been carefully customized to provide a smooth first-boot experience that exemplifies AcreetionOS's commitment to user-friendliness without sacrificing Arch Linux's power. Darren's expertise in CI/CD pipelines ensures that ISO generation and mirror infrastructure operate reliably. The distribution features XLibre alongside the traditional Cinnamon desktop, offering users choice in their computing experience.

Recent community activity includes the intelligence sync operations that keep our newsletter archives and wiki guides current. The security-focused approach extends beyond just the operating system to encompass all infrastructure components. GitLab administrators should remember to direct support requests to our Discord community for the fastest response times.

Looking ahead, the development focus remains on stability and privacy features that align with our community values. The team continues optimizing the build process while preparing for future enhancements to the desktop experience. We appreciate all contributors who help make AcreetionOS a thriving, community-driven project built for and by people who care about software freedom.
